[37] V. ensure that its employees and advisers comply with the obligations of non-disclosure arising from this Agreement;
[38] 3. Either Party shall have the right to refuse to accept any Information under this Agreement prior to any disclosure and nothing herein shall obligate either Party to disclose any particular Information.

- nda-10 (Confidentiality of Agreement): No mention of not disclosing the fact of the agreement. NotMentioned.
- nda-4 (Limited use): Segment [35] says use Information only for Business Purpose unless prior written consent. Entailment, evidence [35].
- nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): Segment [30] mentions required disclosure by law but no notification obligation. NotMentioned.
- nda-12 (Permissible development): Segment [29] excludes independently developed information. Entailment, evidence [29].
- nda-19 (Survival): Segment [47] obligations survive termination for two years. Entailment, evidence [47].
- nda-3 (Verbally conveyed information): Segment [25] defines Information broadly ("information relating to one party which is made available"), including but not limited to technical documentation, etc. This suggests verbal information could be included. Entailment, evidence [25].
- nda-16 (Return of confidential information): Segments [39]-[40] require return or destruction upon request. Entailment, evidence [39, 40].
- nda-1 (Explicit identification): No requirement that information be expressly identified/marked. NotMentioned.
- nda-15 (No licensing): Segments [42]-[43] no rights conferred, no license granted. Entailment, evidence [42, 43].
- nda-7 (Sharing with third-parties): Segment [34] allows sharing with advisers, subsidiaries, affiliates who need to know. Entailment, evidence [34].
- nda-20 (Post-agreement possession): No mention of retention after return/destruction. NotMentioned.
- nda-11 (No reverse engineering): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-17 (Permissible copy): Segment [36] says "nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form" — this prohibits copies. So hypothesis "may create a copy in some circumstances" is Contradiction, evidence [36].
- nda-13 (Acquirement of similar information from third party): Segment [28] excludes information available from a source other than Disclosing Party not bound by confidentiality. Entailment, evidence [28].
- nda-2 (Only technical information): Segment [25] says "including but not limited to technical documentation..." — so not only technical. Contradiction, evidence [25].
- nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Segment [34] allows sharing with employees who need to know. Entailment, evidence [34].
- nda-18 (No solicitation): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

Let me verify a few uncertain ones with human feedback: nda-17 (copy prohibition), nda-3 (verbal information), nda-13.
